Question: Mr. Earl E. Bird leaves his house for work at exactly \(8{:}00\) A.M. every morning. When he averages \(40\) miles per hour, he arrives at his workplace three minutes late. When he averages \(60\) miles per hour, he arrives three minutes early. At what average speed, in miles per hour, should Mr. Bird drive to arrive at his workplace precisely on time?
Solution:
For a fixed distance, increasing the speed decreases the travel time in the inverse ratio. Thus the travel times at \(40\) and \(60\) miles per hour are in the ratio
\[
60:40=3:2.
\]
The slower trip ends three minutes late and the faster trip ends three minutes early, so their travel times differ by six minutes. In the ratio \(3:2\), that difference is one part. Each part is therefore six minutes, making the travel times \(18\) and \(12\) minutes.

To arrive on time, Mr. Bird must take \(18-3=15\) minutes. His distance to work is
\[
40\cdot\frac{18}{60}=12\text{ miles}.
\]
Since fifteen minutes is \(\frac14\) hour, the required speed is
\[
12\div\frac14=\boxed{48}
\]
miles per hour, choice B.
